AccessTokenOut.description: POST /auth/refresh result — a fresh access token only.
AccessTokenOut.title: AccessTokenOut

AlertOut.description: An official air-raid alert window (тривога -> відбій).
AlertOut.title: AlertOut

AnalyzeIn.description: POST /analysis — analyse a target for a card.
AnalyzeIn.title: AnalyzeIn

AnalyzeOut.description: A successful analysis: the card that dropped.
AnalyzeOut.title: AnalyzeOut

AxisOut.description:
A directional threat axis for the map's screen-edge wedge layer. Bearing
and origin display name are derived server-side from the curated origins
table (app/domain/origins.py) — the client just draws the wedge.
AxisOut.title: AxisOut

CardCountOut.description: One collected card + how many copies the user has.
CardCountOut.title: CardCountOut

CollectionOut.description: GET /analysis/collection — the current user's whole card collection.
CollectionOut.title: CollectionOut

CorrectionOut.description:
GET /admin/corrections — a harvested correction plus whether the CURRENT
parser already agrees (so the admin sees which mistakes are retired).
CorrectionOut.title: CorrectionOut

CoverageGapOut.description:
GET /admin/coverage_gaps — a threat-flavored message the parser couldn't
localize (likely a missing gazetteer entry).
CoverageGapOut.title: CoverageGapOut

DismissedOut.description:
GET /admin/dismissed — recently admin-cancelled entities, for the
'Повернути' (restore) list in the admin panel.
DismissedOut.title: DismissedOut

EventDistrictIn.description: PATCH /admin/events/{id} — admin fixes a mislocated sighting.
EventDistrictIn.title: EventDistrictIn

FeedEntryOut.description:
One event feed row: the sighting plus its track's current derived state,
for the frontend event log to hydrate on page load (see /events/recent).
FeedEntryOut.title: FeedEntryOut

FriendActionOut.description:
Result of a friend-graph mutation. The client re-fetches the lists after,
so this only needs to say WHAT happened (used to phrase a toast).
FriendActionOut.title: FriendActionOut

FriendOut.description:
An accepted friend. `home` is populated ONLY when that friend has both set
a home AND turned sharing on — otherwise null (they stay listed, no marker).
FriendOut.title: FriendOut

FriendRequestOut.description: One pending friend request, from the current user's point of view.
FriendRequestOut.title: FriendRequestOut

FriendUserBrief.description: Minimal public identity of another user, for friend lists / requests.
FriendUserBrief.title: FriendUserBrief

GamificationPrefIn.description: PUT /me/gamification — flip the account-bound gamification toggle.
GamificationPrefIn.title: GamificationPrefIn

GazetteerCandidateIn.description:
POST /admin/gazetteer_candidates — flag a toponym from a coverage gap.
NOT a live gazetteer edit; just a captured candidate for later review.
GazetteerCandidateIn.title: GazetteerCandidateIn

GoogleAuthIn.description: POST /auth/google — the id_token from Google Identity Services.
GoogleAuthIn.title: GoogleAuthIn

HomePointOut.description: A friend's shared home coordinates — a map marker only (no radius).
HomePointOut.title: HomePointOut

HomeShareIn.description: PUT /me/home — set/update home coordinates and the share flag together.
HomeShareIn.title: HomeShareIn

HomeZoneIn.description:
The home zone this subscription wants guarded (mirrors the client's
localStorage home — see frontend store/homeSlice.ts).
HomeZoneIn.title: HomeZoneIn

IncidentOut.description: A coordinated attack with counts aggregated from its member threats.
IncidentOut.title: IncidentOut

JournalAlertWindowOut.description:
One тривога→відбій window within a journal day. `seconds` stays 0 for an
incomplete window (still open / failsafe-closed) so it can never be picked
as the day's longest.
JournalAlertWindowOut.title: JournalAlertWindowOut

JournalDayOut.description:
One calendar day of aggregated threat activity — see GET /journal/days.
Mirrors app/domain/journal.py::DayStat. The intensity score is derived on
the client from these fields (the frontend owns the weighting).
JournalDayOut.title: JournalDayOut

JournalOut.description:
GET /journal/days — every day in [from_date, to_date] inclusive, with
zero-activity days present (as empty stats) so the calendar renders gaps.
JournalOut.title: JournalOut

MyHomeOut.description: GET /me/home — the current user's own stored home + share state.
MyHomeOut.title: MyHomeOut

NoticeOut.description: A non-threat feed notice (all-clear / attack summary) for the event log.
NoticeOut.title: NoticeOut

PresencePrefIn.description: PUT /me/presence — opt in/out of showing friends WHEN you were last active.
PresencePrefIn.title: PresencePrefIn

PushConfigOut.description:
GET /push/config — whether push is configured server-side, and the VAPID
public key the browser needs for pushManager.subscribe. Fetched at runtime
so key rotation never requires a frontend rebuild.
PushConfigOut.title: PushConfigOut

PushPrefsIn.description:
Notification preferences (phase 1). Defaults reproduce the pre-0.10
behavior (warning floor, every type) plus the citywide push on.
PushPrefsIn.title: PushPrefsIn

PushSubscribeIn.description:
POST /push/subscribe body. Upsert by endpoint; re-POSTed on every home
or prefs change so the server copy never goes stale.
PushSubscribeIn.title: PushSubscribeIn

RawCountOut.description: How many raw messages match the current /raw filter set.
RawCountOut.title: RawCountOut

RawEventLinkOut.description:
One ThreatEvent a raw message produced — the same T{threat_id}/
M{event_id} pair shown as a dev badge in the feed. A single raw message
can produce SEVERAL (e.g. an untyped "дорозвідка" closing multiple open
tracks at once), hence a list on RawMessageOut rather than one pair.
RawEventLinkOut.title: RawEventLinkOut

RawExportOut.description:
All raw messages matching the current filter (up to the export cap),
for offline analysis — see GET /raw_messages/export. `truncated` flags a
partial export so it's never mistaken for the complete set.
RawExportOut.title: RawExportOut

RawLlmStatsOut.description:
Aggregate LLM fallback usage across all raw messages — see
GET /raw_messages/llm_stats.
RawLlmStatsOut.title: RawLlmStatsOut

RawMessageOut.description:
One verbatim ingested message plus a debug diagnosis of what the
pipeline did with it — see GET /raw_messages. `outcome`/`events`/
`notice_id` are authoritative when a real ThreatEvent/Notice matched
('подія'/'нотіс'); a best-effort re-derived label otherwise (see
api/raw_diagnosis.py).
RawMessageOut.title: RawMessageOut

RawMessagesPage.description: Cursor-paginated page of raw messages, newest first.
RawMessagesPage.title: RawMessagesPage

RawSourceOut.description: One monitored channel, for the /raw channel filter dropdown.
RawSourceOut.title: RawSourceOut

RefreshIn.description: POST /auth/refresh — exchange a refresh token for a new access token.
RefreshIn.title: RefreshIn

ReprocessResultOut.description: POST /admin/reprocess/apply — before/after diff + raw replay counts.
ReprocessResultOut.title: ReprocessResultOut

ReprocessSummaryOut.description:
Snapshot used to diff a reprocess: totals + recent per-day target counts
(where the phantom-count inflation like the 23.07 '432 цілі' shows up).
ReprocessSummaryOut.title: ReprocessSummaryOut

SendFriendRequestIn.description: POST /friends/requests — address a friend request by their email.
SendFriendRequestIn.title: SendFriendRequestIn

ShareToggleIn.description: PATCH /me/home/share — flip sharing without touching coordinates.
ShareToggleIn.title: ShareToggleIn

SourceDeleteOut.description: What a hard-delete removed — surfaced so the admin sees the blast radius.
SourceDeleteOut.title: SourceDeleteOut

SourceIn.description: Add (or reactivate) a channel from the admin console.
SourceIn.title: SourceIn

SourceStatsOut.description:
Per-source quality signals, computed on-demand (JOIN by source_id) over a
recent window — see app/api/source_stats.py. Rates are None when there's no
denominator (e.g. llm_fallback_rate before any row had llm_attempted set).
SourceStatsOut.title: SourceStatsOut

TelegramAuthIn.description:
POST /auth/telegram — the Telegram Login Widget payload. extra='allow'
so any future widget field is preserved for the HMAC data-check-string
(which must include EXACTLY the fields Telegram signed).
TelegramAuthIn.title: TelegramAuthIn

ThreatAnalysisStateOut.description:
GET /analysis/threat/{id} — which analyses this target has left, and which
(if any) the current user already claimed. Drives the inspect-badge button:
`*_taken` disables it globally, `mine.*` shows the card the user won.
ThreatAnalysisStateOut.title: ThreatAnalysisStateOut

ThreatTypeIn.description: PATCH /admin/threats/{id} — admin retype of a track's target.
ThreatTypeIn.title: ThreatTypeIn

TokenPairOut.description: Access + refresh tokens plus the user they belong to.
TokenPairOut.title: TokenPairOut

get.description:
Harvested corrections + whether the CURRENT parser already agrees — so
the operator sees which mistakes are retired vs still reproduced.

schema.title: Response Admin Corrections Admin Corrections Get

get.description:
Recent threat-flavored messages the parser couldn't pin to a district —
the coverage-gap queue (usually a missing gazetteer entry).

schema.title: Response Admin Coverage Gaps Admin Coverage Gaps Get

get.description:
Recently admin-cancelled threats / incidents / alerts, for the restore
('Повернути') list in the admin panel.

delete.description:
Remove a wrongly-attributed sighting. If it was the track's last event,
the now-empty track is dismissed; otherwise the parent incident's type is
recomputed from what remains.

patch.description:
Reassign a sighting to a different district (fix a mislocation). The
threat's vector/geometry are derived from its events at serialization, so a
re-broadcast is all that's needed to update the map.

schema.title: Response Admin List Gazetteer Candidates Admin Gazetteer Candidates Get

post.description:
Capture a toponym candidate from a gap — NOT a live gazetteer edit; that
stays a reviewed code step with a stem-collision sweep (CLAUDE.md).

Wipe + rebuild all tracks/incidents from raw_messages through the current
pipeline. Held under `ingest_lock` so the live listener can't ingest into a
half-rebuilt DB (messages queue behind it and process after). Refuses while
an attack is active unless `force`. raw_messages are preserved, so a
reprocess is repeatable.

get.description:
Pre-flight scope: how many raw messages will replay, the current counts
that will be rebuilt, and whether an attack is active (a reprocess would be
ill-timed). Read-only. Uses reprocess's own SessionLocal so it reads exactly
the DB the apply would rebuild.

Every source with its on-demand quality stats — active channels first,
then by name. Inactive rows are kept (removal is a soft deactivate) so the
operator can re-enable or inspect a channel's history.

schema.title: Response Admin List Sources Admin Sources Get

post.description:
Add (or reactivate) a channel and tell the listener to re-subscribe. Whether
it actually starts delivering shows up as message counts / last_listener_error
on the next connect.

delete.description:
HARD-delete a channel AND all of its stored data (raw_messages, notices,
threat_events), repairing the tracks/incidents it touched — irreversible,
unlike deactivate. Refused while an attack is active (the graph surgery would
disrupt live tracking) unless `force`.

parameters.description: Delete even while an attack is active
parameters.name: force

schema.description: Delete even while an attack is active
schema.title: Force

patch.description:
Edit a source's name / role / trust_weight / active flag. Only a change that
affects what's watched (role or is_active) triggers a listener reload.

post.description:
Remove a channel from the live feed (soft — the row stays, since
raw_messages/threat_events reference it and its history stays queryable).

get.description:
Currently open official alert windows (usually 0 or 1 per scope —
city and oblast can be open independently).

schema.title: Response Active Alerts Alerts Active Get
Response Recent Alerts Alerts Recent Get

Stateless: the client discards its tokens. Endpoint exists for symmetry
and a future server-side revocation hook.

Live directional threat axes (not yet expired), newest first — the map's
screen-edge wedge layer. Supplementary, volunteer-sourced; never the alert.

Another user's collection — visible only to that user themselves or an
accepted friend (collections aren't public).
Real OSM boundary polygons for districts that have one (the 10 raions).

Most recent sightings across ALL tracks (open or closed), newest first —
hydrates the frontend event feed on page load (it otherwise only grows from
live WebSocket traffic and empties on every reload).

schema.title: Response Recent Events Events Recent Get

get.description:
Ongoing attacks (incidents not yet ended), each with counts aggregated
over its member threats — the "one attack" rollup for the UI summary strip.

schema.title: Response Active Incidents Incidents Active Get

get.description:
Most recent attacks (ended or active), newest first — hydrates the feed's
attack-summary cards on load so an incident that ended before the client
connected still renders its rollup.

schema.title: Response Recent Incidents Incidents Recent Get

get.description:
Per-day threat activity for the journal calendar: attacks, targets,
target-type mix, alert duration and districts touched, one row per day in
[from, to] inclusive (zero-activity days included). Days are bucketed by
Europe/Kyiv local date. The SQL only bounds the range; all bucketing happens
in Python (see domain/journal.py) — no tz-fragile SQL date math.

parameters.description: End day (Kyiv), YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today
parameters.name: to

schema.title: To

put.description: Persist the account-bound gamification toggle so it syncs across devices.

Opt in/out of disclosing WHEN you were last active. Turning it off hides
the timestamp immediately; it does not stop `last_seen_at` being recorded,
since the online dot is derived from the same field.

get.description:
Recent non-threat notices (all-clears / attack summaries), newest first —
the frontend interleaves them into the event feed as info entries.

schema.title: Response Recent Notices Notices Recent Get

get.description:
Whether Web Push is configured server-side + the VAPID public key for
pushManager.subscribe. The frontend hides its notification control when
enabled=false.

delete.description: Idempotent: deleting an unknown endpoint is a no-op success.

post.description:
Register (or update — upsert by endpoint) a push subscription with its
home zone. Re-POSTed on every home change; moving home resets the per-track
danger bookkeeping so levels computed for the OLD location can't suppress
fresh pushes for the new one. When the request carries a valid token, the
subscription is stamped with the owner so a user's devices can be linked.

get.description:
Every ingested message verbatim, INCLUDING ones the parser suppressed
or couldn't localize — a debug view onto the pipeline, distinct from
/events/recent (which only shows messages that became a live sighting).
Cursor-paginated (before_id) newest-first — raw_messages can run to tens
of thousands of rows, too many to offset-paginate cheaply.

parameters.description: Substring search over message text, OR one/more T{id}/M{id}/N{id} codes (the same dev badges shown in the feed) to look up by exact match instead
parameters.name: q

get.description:
How many raw messages match the current filter set — powers the
"показано N з M" counter on /raw without paging through everything.

Every message matching the current filter (up to _RAW_EXPORT_CAP), for
offline analysis. Returned oldest-first so the export reads as a sequence
of events; the frontend wraps these in a JSON envelope with the human
filter description before download.

Aggregate LLM fallback usage across ALL raw messages — total calls,
tokens, and cost, for the analytics strip on /raw. Unfiltered (ignores
search/outcome filters) so it always reads as "overall spend", not
"spend within the current view".

Channels that actually have stored raw messages, for the /raw channel
filter dropdown. DB-driven now (subscription moved off the env lists), so it
lists every source with data — active or not — instead of the env-configured
set, which is empty once TELEGRAM_CHANNELS/ALERT_CHANNELS are cleared.

schema.title: Response Raw Messages Sources Raw Messages Sources Get

get.description:
Tracks that are not yet closed (still tracking / unconfirmed), plus
RECENT `impact` markers — those are closed-on-creation (a strike is terminal)
but persist on the map as confirmed-hit pins. Only impacts within
`impact_map_ttl_hours` are returned, so strikes from days-old attacks don't
accumulate on the live map (history/feed keep them regardless).

schema.title: Response Active Threats Threats Active Get
Response Threat Events Threats  Threat Id  Events Get
